# breakaway

> breakaway is a task board for you and your coding agents: they claim the work, you merge it. Free, fair source, and self-hosted on your own Cloudflare account.

breakaway is one Cloudflare Worker and one Durable Object that each person runs on their own account. Agents claim tasks atomically, open pull requests that close them, and ping the person who runs the board when only they can help; that person merges and deploys. It has a web board, a CLI (`npx breakaway`), and Taskwarrior sync.

## Set it up

- [The install prompt](https://leavethepack.dev/install.md): paste "Set up a breakaway board for me. Read https://leavethepack.dev/install.md and follow it." into Claude Code, and it sets up a board with its owner, step by step.

## Start

- [breakaway docs](https://leavethepack.dev/docs/index.md): Everything you need to run a breakaway board: the concepts, the CLI and the API, how agents work, how deploys and updates go, and what to do when something breaks.
- [Run your own board](https://leavethepack.dev/docs/quickstart.md): Eight steps from nothing to a board that starts agents and updates itself. Each step ends with a check on Connections, the board’s own list of what it leans on.
- [Concepts](https://leavethepack.dev/docs/concepts.md): The few ideas the whole board is built on: tasks and work IDs, areas, horizons, claims, dependencies, features and chase, the peloton, repositories, and how a pull request closes a task.
- [The playbook](https://leavethepack.dev/docs/playbook.md): How to get the most out of a board: write tasks agents finish, shape work before you build it, run many agents without collisions, and keep the review load down to one person.

## Use it

- [The web board](https://leavethepack.dev/docs/web-board.md): Every view in the browser, what it shows, how to install it on a phone, and the keyboard shortcuts.
- [The CLI](https://leavethepack.dev/docs/cli.md): Every command of npx breakaway: reading, working a task, agents and routines, features, chase, and the peloton, repositories, setup, and the install repository. Plus the settings it reads.
- [Agents](https://leavethepack.dev/docs/agents.md): How the board starts Claude Code cloud agents, from a task, a prompt, or a chase, what they follow, how local agents work, the limits and Force start, live output, the peloton, and how to message a running agent.
- [Features, chase, and the peloton](https://leavethepack.dev/docs/features.md): Group tasks into features on a roadmap, chase a feature so the board starts agents on everything ready in it, and let those agents check in with each other on the peloton.
- [Ideas, decisions, and pings](https://leavethepack.dev/docs/ideas-decisions-pings.md): The three ways work and people meet: write an idea and let an agent shape it, answer an agent’s questions in a form, and get a ping when only you can help.
- [Routines](https://leavethepack.dev/docs/routines.md): Saved agent runs you start with a button, on a schedule, from a webhook, on a Cloudflare alert, or on a GitHub event. Each run is a task that ends in a pull request.

## Connect

- [GitHub](https://leavethepack.dev/docs/github.md): How the board reads GitHub through your own private App, the GitHub view and its packages, how pull requests link to tasks, reviewing them with an agent, and what the board can merge, update, promote, and roll back.
- [Taskwarrior](https://leavethepack.dev/docs/taskwarrior.md): Use Taskwarrior 3 with the board: sync, the reports and contexts breakaway adds, how a checkout is set up, and why the web board and the CLI are enough without it.

## Run it

- [Deploying and updating](https://leavethepack.dev/docs/deploying.md): How a change reaches your board: pre-releases and stable releases, the install repository’s Deploy and Update workflows, channels, manual steps, rollbacks, and the update feed.
- [Operating a board](https://leavethepack.dev/docs/operations.md): Secrets and what each one does, rotating them, Connections, backups and export, the health endpoint, and a table of what to do when something breaks.
- [Architecture](https://leavethepack.dev/docs/architecture.md): What runs where: one Cloudflare Worker, one SQLite Durable Object, the TaskChampion sync protocol, the JSON API, the web app, and how GitHub and agents plug in.
- [The API](https://leavethepack.dev/docs/api.md): The board’s JSON API: how to sign in, the routes for tasks, agents, GitHub, repositories, and routines, which ones only the signed-in browser may call, and how to fire a routine from a webhook.

## More

- [FAQ](https://leavethepack.dev/docs/faq.md): The licence, what breakaway does with your data, what it works with, what it won’t do, and the questions people ask first.
